title: What was America's first terrorist threat?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the origin of the word terrorism (coined during the French Revolution's Reign of Terror) and argue that America's first terrorist threat was Barbary Coast piracy. They cover Mediterranean piracy from the Barbarossa brothers onward, the extortion and tribute system paid by European and US governments, Franklin's 1786-era diplomacy and the 1787 Treaty of Amity and Commerce, Jefferson's presidency and the First Barbary War (1801-1805) including the capture and recapture of the USS Philadelphia by Stephen Decatur, the Second Barbary War under Monroe, and the Mathurian order that ransomed sailors, including Miguel de Cervantes. The episode also includes a Science Channel TV show plug, a listener sexuality email, and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the show with banter and note that terrorism comes from the French, coined during the Reign of Terror.

segments.title: Defining terrorism and early hijackings
segments.summary: The hosts define terrorism as targeting citizens and note that terrorism became a household word by the 1960s and 1980s, especially with airplane hijackings. They frame piracy as early terrorism.

segments.title: Barbary brothers and Mediterranean piracy
segments.summary: The Barbarossa brothers, Turkish-born pirates helping Muslims expelled from Spain, gave their name to the Barbary Coast. The Mediterranean became a piracy haven along the spice trade route.

segments.title: Captures, extortion and tribute
segments.summary: Barbary pirates captured ships and crews, held captives for ransom or sold them as slaves, and extracted tribute from European nations, which built the payments into their budgets. Nations paid tribute on a sliding scale.

segments.title: US tribute and the birth of the Navy
segments.summary: The new US paid tribute to Barbary states, starting at about $80,000 and rising to a million dollars a year for fifteen years. Jefferson argued a navy would be cheaper, and the tribute drove the creation of the US Navy. Franklin's earlier 1778 treaty with France referenced the Barbary nations.

segments.title: First Barbary War
segments.summary: Jefferson, as president, refused to keep paying and sent ships against Tripoli. The USS Philadelphia ran aground and was captured and used as a gun battery; Lieutenant Stephen Decatur led Marines to recapture and burn it. The war ran 1801 to 1805, mostly at sea.

segments.title: Second Barbary War and end of tribute
segments.summary: Under James Monroe, the US took a more aggressive stance against Tunis and Algiers, bombarding their cities, after which the US stopped paying tribute. The hosts note US use of local mercenaries in the First War.

segments.title: Mathurian ransom and Cervantes
segments.summary: The French Catholic Mathurian order raised money to ransom captured sailors, freeing around 90,000 over three centuries, including Miguel de Cervantes. The hosts also discuss slavery in Africa compared to European-style slavery.

segments.title: Science Channel TV show plug
segments.summary: Hosts promote their Science Channel television show premiere and episode two, and the iTunes availability.

segments.title: Listener mail: sexual healing
segments.summary: An anonymous listener thanks the show for its episode on sexuality, sharing how it helped him come to terms with his sexual orientation. The hosts close with how to contact the show.
